references_named: Hendrik Lenstra, mathematical completion of Escher's Print Gallery (2003)
net.art (the page as its own material)
rationale: The mechanism — srcdoc-ing the page's own outerHTML into a nesting iframe — is genuinely web-native and elegantly enacts the Escher recursion. However, the candidate is materially the same work as 'Print Gallery (The Part It Cannot Draw)' already listed in the candidate catalogue (2026) under the same title, same references (Escher, Droste, Lenstra), same mechanism (iframe srcdoc feeding outerHTML, browser frame-nesting limit as the hole). G6 fails on duplicate. Conceptually the piece is strong: P1 holds well — the nesting limit IS the blank centre, not depicted but enacted. Restraint is good. But novelty over the existing entry is zero, so the scored novelty reflects mechanism-quality rather than new-found-object/origin.
reservations: G6 fails: candidate is a duplicate of the already-catalogued 'Print Gallery (The Part It Cannot Draw) (2026)'. No new ontology, no new found-object versus the existing entry. The depth limit (MAX=8) and transform values may differ cosmetically from the archived version, but source, mechanism, and argument are identical.
revision_suggestion: To clear G6, either (a) submit genuinely different recursion mechanics — e.g., nest via CSS conic-gradient or a custom-element tree rather than srcdoc iframes, or (b) reframe the source from 'Escher's blank hole' to a distinct self-referential lineage (e.g., Quine / fixed-point combinators, or Hofstadter's strange-loop reading), or (c) merge into the existing Print Gallery entry and remove as a separate work.
